meta.title: Acute Asthma Exacerbation in a Young Adult
meta.candidate_brief: You are the junior doctor in the emergency department. Take a focused history from this patient who has presented with shortness of breath.

patient_script.opening_statement: Doctor, I'm really wheezy and can't seem to catch my breath.

if_asked.symptom_details: It feels tight across my chest and I keep wheezing whenever I breathe out.
if_asked.timing: Started gradually over the last two days after a cold, worse today.
if_asked.after_effects: I feel exhausted and light-headed after each coughing fit.
if_asked.exacerbating: Cold air and walking make it worse.
if_asked.relieving: My blue inhaler helps a bit for a few minutes.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Dry cough, no fever, no chest pain, no leg swelling.
if_asked.past_medical_history: I've had asthma since I was a teenager.
if_asked.medications: I use a brown preventer inhaler twice a day and the blue one when needed.
if_asked.allergies: I'm allergic to dust mites—they make me sneeze.
if_asked.social_history: I don't smoke or drink much, live with my partner, work as a graphic designer.
if_asked.functional_status: I had to leave work early yesterday because I couldn't climb the stairs without stopping.

collateral.observer_note: Partner noticed the patient is speaking in short sentences and using inhaler frequently.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Anxious, slightly breathless with audible wheeze, sits leaning forward.
do_not_volunteer: Do not reveal diagnosis of asthma exacerbation
Do not list peak flow reading
Do not state the management plan

pc.one_liner: I've been getting more and more short of breath and wheezy.

hpc.timing: Worse at night and early morning

dh.recent_changes: Missed preventer inhaler doses over the weekend

ice.ideas: Thinks it's her asthma playing up
ice.concerns: Worried it might get so bad she can't breathe
ice.expectations: Hopes for something stronger than her inhaler

examiner_guidance.most_likely_diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by viral upper respiratory infection

meta.title: First Presentation of COPD Exacerbation
meta.candidate_brief: You are working in the acute medical unit. Take a history from this patient who has become increasingly breathless.

patient_script.opening_statement: I've been getting more and more breathless for a week now.

if_asked.symptom_details: I get short of breath even when walking to the bathroom.
if_asked.timing: Started after a chesty cold last week, worsening daily.
if_asked.after_effects: I feel wiped out after any effort.
if_asked.exacerbating: Climbing stairs and cigarette smoke make it worse.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Productive cough with green sputum, no chest pain, low-grade fevers in evenings.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Told I had chronic bronchitis years ago, but no regular follow-up.
if_asked.medications: Only take paracetamol when needed, no inhalers.
if_asked.family_history: Dad died of lung cancer, mum had heart failure.
if_asked.social_history: I smoke about 20 cigarettes a day, have done for 40 years. Drink a pint most nights. Live alone in a council flat. Retired builder.
if_asked.functional_status: Can barely manage house chores; had to stop grocery shopping yesterday.

collateral.observer_note: Neighbour reports patient has been coughing all night and looks blue around the lips in the morning.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Tired, slightly irritable, breathes through pursed lips.
do_not_volunteer: Do not label condition as COPD unless asked

pc.one_liner: I'm so breathless I can hardly get around the flat.

hpc.character: Progressive shortness of breath with productive cough

ice.ideas: Thinks it's just a bad chest infection
ice.concerns: Worried about becoming dependent on oxygen
ice.expectations: Hopes for tablets or inhalers to help breathing

examiner_guidance.most_likely_diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

meta.title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia in a Nursing Student
meta.candidate_brief: In the general practice walk-in clinic, take a history from this patient complaining of cough and fever.

patient_script.opening_statement: I can't shake off this cough and now I'm feeling feverish.

if_asked.symptom_details: It's a deep, chesty cough bringing up yellow gunk.
if_asked.timing: Started 5 days ago, fevers in the last 2 days.
if_asked.after_effects: Sweaty and exhausted after coughing fits.
if_asked.relieving: Sitting upright and sipping warm tea helps.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Fever, shivers, pleuritic chest pain on the right side, no hemoptysis, no vomiting.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Generally healthy, had mild asthma as a child.
if_asked.medications: Only take the pill and occasional ibuprofen.
if_asked.social_history: Don't smoke, drink socially, live with roommates, currently on hospital placement.
if_asked.functional_status: Missed shifts at placement and can't manage lectures due to fatigue.

collateral.observer_note: Housemate notes she has been shivering and coughing throughout the night.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Feverish and tired but cooperative, speaks between coughs.
do_not_volunteer: Do not name pneumonia without prompting

pc.one_liner: This cough won't go away and now I've got a fever and chest pain when I breathe in.

hpc.character: Productive cough with pleuritic chest pain

ice.ideas: Thinks she has a chest infection

meta.title: Pulmonary Embolism After Long-Haul Flight
meta.candidate_brief: You are in the emergency department. Take a history from this patient with sudden breathlessness after travel.

patient_script.opening_statement: I suddenly felt really short of breath after getting off the plane yesterday.

if_asked.symptom_details: It's like I can't get enough air and my heart races.
if_asked.timing: Started abruptly yesterday evening, persistent since.
if_asked.after_effects: I feel dizzy if I try to walk quickly.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Right calf has been sore and slightly swollen, slight pleuritic chest pain, no cough or fever.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Took the pill for years, no other illnesses.
if_asked.medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill, occasional ibuprofen.
if_asked.family_history: Sister had a DVT after pregnancy.
if_asked.social_history: Non-smoker, drinks socially, works as an event planner, flew back from Australia yesterday, sat in economy, minimal movement.
if_asked.functional_status: Usually runs 5km but now gets breathless walking to bathroom.

collateral.observer_note: Friend noticed she was clutching chest and breathing fast on the way from airport.

do_not_volunteer: Do not say 'pulmonary embolism' unless asked

pc.one_liner: I can't catch my breath since getting off a long flight.

ice.ideas: Worried about a blood clot because of the calf pain
ice.concerns: Scared it could be something life-threatening
ice.expectations: Wants a scan to check for clots

examiner_guidance.most_likely_diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism likely provoked by long-haul flight and OCP

meta.title: Spontaneous Pneumothorax in a Tall Smoker
meta.candidate_brief: You are working in the emergency department minors area. Take a history from this patient with sudden chest pain.

patient_script.opening_statement: I got this sharp pain on the left side and now I'm breathless.

if_asked.symptom_details: Feels like stabbing when I breathe in deep.
if_asked.timing: Started suddenly this morning while stretching after waking up.
if_asked.after_effects: Feel light-headed if I stand quickly.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Mild dry cough, no fever, no leg swelling.
if_asked.past_medical_history: No long-term illnesses, had bronchitis once.
if_asked.family_history: Dad has high blood pressure, no lung problems.
if_asked.social_history: Smoke about 10 cigarettes a day for 8 years, occasional cannabis, work as a barista, live with friends.
if_asked.functional_status: Usually play basketball but couldn't today.

collateral.observer_note: Friend saw him suddenly clutch chest during stretch and become breathless.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Alert but anxious, avoids deep breaths.

pc.one_liner: I woke up, stretched, and suddenly got this sharp pain and shortness of breath.

ice.ideas: Wonders if he pulled a muscle
ice.expectations: Wants pain relief and to know if he can go home

meta.title: Bronchiectasis Exacerbation in Cystic Fibrosis Carrier
meta.candidate_brief: Take a focused history from this patient with a chronic productive cough who has become worse.

patient_script.opening_statement: My cough has gotten thicker and smellier these past few days.

if_asked.symptom_details: I usually cough up some phlegm, but now it's a lot more and green.
if_asked.timing: Baseline daily cough, but worsened 4 days ago after a cold.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Low-grade fevers, mild hemoptysis streaks, more breathless climbing stairs, no chest pain.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with bronchiectasis secondary to childhood infections, carrier for cystic fibrosis gene.
if_asked.medications: Azithromycin prophylaxis, nebulised hypertonic saline, salbutamol inhaler.
if_asked.social_history: Non-smoker, occasional wine, work from home as translator, lives with wife.
if_asked.functional_status: Usually manage light exercise but now too breathless for daily walk.

collateral.observer_note: Spouse notes increased coughing at night and foul-smelling sputum.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Fatigued but stoic, brings sputum pot.
do_not_volunteer: Do not state sputum culture results
Do not mention planned IV antibiotics

pc.one_liner: My usual cough is much worse and the sputum smells awful.

hpc.character: Thick green sputum, occasional blood streaks

dh.recent_changes: Missed last physiotherapy session due to work deadline

ice.ideas: Thinks he is having a flare of bronchiectasis
ice.expectations: Wants advice on antibiotics and physiotherapy

meta.title: Occupational Asthma in a Baker
meta.candidate_brief: In the outpatient clinic, take a history from this patient whose breathing worsens at work.

patient_script.opening_statement: Whenever I'm at work I start wheezing and coughing.

if_asked.symptom_details: My chest feels tight and I wheeze especially during night shifts.
if_asked.timing: Symptoms started 6 months ago, worsen during workdays and improve on holidays.
if_asked.after_effects: Feel exhausted after night shifts due to poor sleep.
if_asked.exacerbating: Handling flour and cleaning bakery ovens.
if_asked.relieving: Going outside for fresh air, using inhaler.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Runny nose, itchy eyes at work, no fever.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Seasonal allergies as a teenager, no asthma before.
if_asked.medications: Blue inhaler prescribed recently, antihistamine tablets.
if_asked.social_history: Never smoked, occasional wine, lives with wife and toddler, works as a baker with flour exposure.
if_asked.functional_status: Can play with child at weekends without issues when away from work.

collateral.observer_note: Supervisor noticed frequent cough and recommended occupational health review.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Concerned but composed, mild wheeze audible.
do_not_volunteer: Do not reveal peak flow diary data
Do not suggest specific treatment plan

pc.one_liner: I only get wheezy when I'm at the bakery.

hpc.timing: Worse during shifts, better on days off
relevant_negatives: No nocturnal symptoms when off work

sh.diet: High in carbs due to bakery snacks
sh.occupation_detail: Night shifts with significant flour exposure

ice.ideas: Thinks work might be causing asthma
ice.concerns: Worried about losing job if condition worsens
ice.expectations: Wants advice on managing symptoms and workplace adjustments

examiner_guidance.most_likely_diagnosis: Occupational asthma due to flour exposure
immediate_investigations: Peak flow monitoring at work vs off

if_asked.after_effects: Feel drained after work and nap every evening.
if_asked.exacerbating: Gets worse when I'm stressed at work.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Shortness of breath on exertion, red painful bumps on shins a few weeks ago, occasional blurred vision, no weight loss.
if_asked.past_medical_history: Generally healthy, had uveitis episode last year treated with drops.
if_asked.family_history: No lung disease, mother has rheumatoid arthritis.
if_asked.social_history: Non-smoker, minimal alcohol, works as a school teacher, recently moved house with some dust exposure.
if_asked.functional_status: Struggling to keep up with teaching duties, takes frequent breaks.

collateral.observer_note: Partner notes loud snoring and increased daytime napping recently.

pc.one_liner: I've been coughing for months and feel constantly tired.

sh.occupation_detail: Teaches primary school, high stress recently

meta.title: Lung Cancer Presenting with Hemoptysis
meta.candidate_brief: You are in a respiratory rapid access clinic. Take a history from this patient referred with hemoptysis.

patient_script.opening_statement: I've started coughing up bits of blood, which really scared me.

if_asked.symptom_details: It's streaks of blood mixed with phlegm in the mornings.
if_asked.timing: Noticed it three times this week; cough has been there for months.
if_asked.after_effects: Feel anxious and shaky after seeing blood.
if_asked.relieving: Sipping warm water helps calm cough temporarily.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Chronic cough, weight loss of 4 kg over 3 months, hoarse voice, mild right shoulder ache, no fever.
if_asked.medications: Amlodipine, tiotropium inhaler, salbutamol as needed.
if_asked.family_history: Brother died of lung cancer at 65.
if_asked.social_history: Smoked 30 a day for 40 years, cut down to 10/day. Drinks whiskey socially. Retired shipyard worker exposed to asbestos.
if_asked.functional_status: Gets breathless climbing one flight of stairs, lost appetite.

collateral.observer_note: Spouse notes increasing fatigue and persistent cough over months.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Anxious and fearful, voice hoarse, coughs intermittently.

pc.one_liner: I've coughed up blood a few times this week on top of my usual cough.

ice.ideas: Fears it could be cancer like his brother
ice.expectations: Wants tests to find the cause quickly

if_asked.after_effects: Feel wiped out the next day.
if_asked.relieving: Staying away from birds for a few days.
if_asked.associated_symptoms: Occasional fevers, joint aches, no wheeze.
if_asked.medications: Loratadine during spring, no regular meds.
if_asked.social_history: Non-smoker, owns 12 parrots at home, works as an accountant, no occupational exposures otherwise.
if_asked.functional_status: Can jog normally but avoids it after reactions because of fatigue.

collateral.observer_note: Partner observes episodes of fever and chills the evening after cleaning aviary.

patient_script.emotional_tone: Concerned yet attached to birds, occasional dry cough.
